Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaMart Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaMart's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Maria Gonzalez, COO; David Kim, CMO; Lisa Patel, CTO; and Raj Singh, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaMart.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by exceptional gross merchandise value growth and accelerating international market expansion. We saw significant growth in key metrics like active buyers reaching 185 million globally and repeat purchase rates hitting a record 68 percent.

Our focus remains on operational efficiency and supply chain resilience amid disruptions. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our new NovaPrime Essentials subscription service and NovaTech private-label electronics line, which we believe will significantly boost customer lifetime value and category penetration.

We are investing heavily in AI-driven personalization and fulfillment network expansions to support this momentum.

We are focused on improving unit economics through better inventory management and cost controls.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like Asia-Pacific and Latin America.

Finally, we are committed to delivering profitable growth and long-term shareholder value.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q3 revenue was $5.68 billion, an increase of 22 percent year-over-year. Gross margin was 41.2 percent, driven by take rate expansion, favorable product mix shifts toward higher-margin categories like electronics, and logistics leverage from our fulfillment optimizations. Operating expenses were $2.74 billion, representing 48.3 percent of revenue, reflecting strong discipline even as we scaled amid inflation and competitive pressures.

Let me start with our headline metric: gross merchandise value, or GMV, which reached $28.4 billion for the quarter, up 17 percent year-over-year and 6.2 percent quarter-over-quarter. This beat our guidance of 14 to 16 percent YoY and 4 to 6 percent QoQ, showcasing the strength of our marketplace amid softer consumer spending and competition from players like Temu and Shein. This growth outpaced the e-commerce industry's 10 to 12 percent average, per eMarketer, and topped peers like Shopify.

Diving deeper, we added 4.2 million net new active buyers QoQ to hit 185 million, up 12 percent YoY, with repeats at 68 percent thanks to NovaAI 2.0 personalization lifting click-throughs 25 percent. Average order value rose 4 percent to $162 via upselling bundles. North America at 52 percent of GMV delivered 19 percent YoY growth to $14.8 billion; Europe 15 percent to $7.9 billion with live-streaming wins; APAC and emerging markets 22 percent to $5.7 billion led by India and Southeast Asia. Categories shone: electronics up 20 percent, fashion 16 percent, grocery 25 percent.

Technical enablers included predictive inventory AI cutting stockouts 40 percent, mobile app GMV at 72 percent with AR try-ons boosting conversions 15 percent, and 150,000 new sellers via our tools. For Q4, we guide 18 to 21 percent YoY GMV growth.

Turning to international expansion, a cornerstone driving over 35 percent of total GMV. Our cross-border strategy delivered $9.94 billion in international GMV, up 145 percent YoY and 38 percent of our $28.4 billion consolidated GMV, ahead of our 30 to 35 percent mix target. This came from organic demand, marketplace integrations, and supply chain tweaks slashing fulfillment times 28 percent.

Regionally, Europe was 42 percent of international at $4.17 billion, up 162 percent YoY, led by UK and Germany with 22 percent market share in fashion and beauty per SimilarWeb. ARPU up 18 percent to €45 via 85 percent localized top SKUs and AI personalization lifting conversions to 4.2 percent and add-to-carts 31 percent. CAC down 22 percent to €18, LTV/CAC at 4.2x despite VAT and Brexit challenges, aided by DHL partnerships.

Asia-Pacific at 38 percent or $3.78 billion, up 210 percent, with India starring at $1.74 billion via UPI and ONDC, mirroring Temu pricing for 5.8 percent conversions and ₹850 ARPU. Southeast Asia added $1.24 billion via TikTok Shop, with Singapore FC enabling 2-3 day delivery, cutting returns 19 percent and repeats to 42 percent; ROAS 8.5x.

Latin America 15 percent or $1.49 billion, up 110 percent despite FX; Brazil $913 million with Mercado Pago BNPL at 28 percent adoption lifting AOV 22 percent to R$250; Mexico ramping with Tijuana warehouse to $35 GMV per user. CAC $12, LTV $85 at 7x, countering higher chargebacks with AI.

Middle East and Africa 5 percent or $497 million, with UAE up 90 percent via noon.com. Take rate steady at 22.5 percent, margins up 240 bps to 41.2 percent as fulfillment costs fell to 14 percent of GMV via robotics and routing. DAUs up 190 percent to 8.2 million, 55 percent mobile. Pillars ahead: gen-AI localization, partnerships like Klarna, sustainability lifting NPS to 68. Expect $5.5 to 6 billion annualized run-rate by year-end, 45 percent mix in FY25.

On operating expenses, we hit $2.74 billion, up 11 percent YoY against 22 percent revenue growth, for a 48.3 percent ratio down 170 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ. Adjusted, it's 47.8 percent excluding restructuring. Leverage from 28 percent GMV growth and efficiencies in fulfillment, marketing, tech, and G&A.

Fulfillment at $1.46 billion or 25.6 percent of revenue, down 250 bps YoY, beating peers amid Red Sea issues and fuel hikes. Automation via Symbotic in 85 percent of 45 NA FCs boosted picks 35 percent, cutting labor 18 percent; stockouts down 28 percent. Owned NovaFulfill at 62 percent of orders dropped CPO to $7.92. US offset wage inflation with Mexico; Europe via Dublin consolidation; APAC drone pilots cut costs 14 percent.

Marketing $826 million or 14.5 percent, CAC to $28 with LTV/CAC 4.2x via TikTok Reels and NovaPrime driving 65 percent repeats; ROAS 5.5x US. Tech/content $296 million or 5.5 percent down 20 bps on AWS savings; G&A $150 million flat at 2.7 percent with headcount up 4 percent.

This supports our efficient scale: AI for CPO savings, micro-FCs, high-margin durables, omnichannel BOPIS. OpEx/revenue below 47 percent FYE.

Take rate expanded 130 bps to 18.5 percent, adding $450 million revenue. Pricing +50 bps via tiered fees 12 to 16 percent and 5-7 percent fulfillment hikes with SFN at 62 percent. Promos -20 bps from SphereFest but optimized via ML. Mix +60 bps from electronics/home at 38 percent; private label +15 bps. Tech +30 bps: fraud cuts refunds to 4.2 percent, ads to 32 percent GMV. NA 17.8 percent, EMEA 20.1 percent, APAC/LATAM 18.9 percent. Q4 to 19.0-19.2 percent.

Net income was $1.12 billion GAAP, or $2.18 diluted EPS, beating consensus $920 million and $1.79 by 22 and 21.8 percent. Adjusted $1.35 billion or $2.65 EPS, up 32 percent YoY. Revenue $5.68 billion up 15 percent beat guide; margins 28.4 percent via AI pricing +8 percent AOV, ads +42 percent. Fulfillment 12.2 percent improved. NA led, APAC accelerated, EMEA resilient. Guide Q3 adj EPS $2.85-2.95, FY $11.20-11.50.

We ended with $4.2 billion in cash. Reaffirming full-year guidance: revenue $22-23 billion, adj EPS $11.00-11.40, GMV $112-115 billion.

Now I'll turn it over to Maria to discuss operations.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment scale amid disruptions. Shipping times improved by 25 percent overall. Fulfillment costs improved 15 percent as a percentage of GMV.

Logistics and shipping hit $1.2 billion, up 28 percent YoY to 18.5 percent of revenue from disruptions like Red Sea reroutes adding 150 percent to ocean rates, US port strikes delaying 25 percent inbound, Panama drought, and labor shortages pushing LTL 15 percent. Inbound Asia 42 percent of surge; last-mile 55 percent up 22 percent on fuel.

NA last-mile $4.85/package up 19 percent; Europe 22 percent on carbon fees; APAC 15 percent despite typhoons. Mitigations: AI TMS with FourKites saving $45 million via 22 percent less deadhead; 120 micro-FCs cutting miles 30 percent; 25 percent nearshoring to Mexico saving 40 percent; WMS turns to 10.5x, stockouts under 2 percent. Dynamic surcharges recover 60 percent costs; drone/Rivian pilots. Q4 to 17 percent, FY $4.8-5.0 billion.

We are implementing advanced robotics and dynamic routing.

Now I'll turn it over to David.

David Kim:
Thanks, Maria. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from SphereFest promotions and TikTok integrations. Customer acquisition costs were $28. Our brand awareness increased by 22 percent. We are focusing on performance channels and loyalty to drive repeats.

Live commerce pilots contributed $95 million GMV at 18 percent take rate, 8.5 percent conversion. NovaPrime NPS 72, 3.5x repeats.

Now I'll turn it over to Lisa.

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, David. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization and mobile enhancements. Our website uptime was 99.99 percent. Mobile app usage increased by 72 percent of GMV. We're investing in AR try-ons and predictive inventory.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj.

Raj Singh:
Thanks, Lisa. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 25 percent improvement in conversion rates because of NovaAI 2.0 initiatives. We are also focusing on privacy-compliant models.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for Q&A: please limit to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter:
Thanks. Great quarter on GMV—can you expand on the international drivers and how you're navigating FX and tariffs?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Emily. As Jordan detailed, international GMV up 145 percent to nearly $10 billion, 38 percent mix. Europe led with 162 percent growth via localization and AI, APAC 210 percent on UPI and social commerce. We're mitigating tariffs with 40 percent nearshoring to Vietnam/Mexico, hedging FX, and partnerships. Confident in 50 percent plus growth ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Patel:
On op ex efficiency, how sustainable is the 48.3 percent ratio with marketing steady?

Jordan Lee:
Mike, sustainability comes from embedded AI across stack for 10-15 percent CPO savings annually, micro-fulfillment, and margin mix. Fulfillment down 250 bps via robotics in 85 percent FCs. Marketing CAC discipline at 4.2x LTV/CAC. Expect below 47 percent FYE despite 3-5 percent carrier hikes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with JPMorgan.

Laura Chen:
Shipping costs up sharply—details on Red Sea impact and mitigation timeline?

Maria Gonzalez:
Laura, Red Sea forced 35 percent reroutes, +150 percent rates to $4,200/FEU. Added $180 million inbound. AI TMS optimizes 65 percent fleet, micro-FCs at 120 total cut miles 30 percent. Nearshoring 25 percent electronics saves 40 percent. Q4 moderates to 17 percent; $200 million savings run-rate by 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Barclays.

Tom Rivera:
Take rate to 18.5 percent impressive—pricing pushback from sellers?

David Kim:
Tom, tiered pricing accretive from top sellers at 14-16 percent with priority visibility. SFN opt-in high at 62 percent despite hikes. Churn minimal at 92 percent retention. Mix and ads like Sponsored Brands 2.0 add tailwinds. Q4 another 50-70 bps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Lee with Citi.

Anna Lee:
Thoughts on new launches like NovaPrime—customer feedback and scaling plans?

Lisa Patel:
Anna, NovaPrime at 1.2 million subs, 22 percent new cohort penetration, NPS 72 vs 58 platform. 3.5x repeats, AOV +25 percent to $145. NovaTech $180 million GMV, 4.2 percent conversion via AR. Live $95 million, 4.9 stars. Scaling to APAC Q4, targeting 20 percent GMV FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Gupta with Deutsche Bank.

Raj Gupta:
Net income beat strong—margin drivers and EPS guide raise factors?

Raj Singh:
Raj, GAAP $1.12 billion net, $2.18 EPS beat 22 percent; adj $1.35 billion, $2.65 up 32 percent YoY. Margins +210 bps to 28.4 percent on AI pricing, ads +42 percent, private label 45 percent. Regional strength, expense control. FY guide up to $11.20-11.50 on momentum.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Take rate: Changes and drivers (e.g., pricing, promotions).
New product or service launches: Early performance and customer feedback.
